svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.21.4.4 Height of Chimney Flues
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.21.4.4 Height of Chimney Flues
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.21 MASONRY AND CONCRETE CHIMNEYS AND FLUES
Height of Chimney Flues

g.text: (a) 900 mm above the highest point where
(a) 900 mm above the roof the chimney
(b) 600 mm above the ridge, the highest
roof surface within 3 m. Here (b) governs.
(b) 600 mm above the roof surface 3 m

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
A chimney flue extends not less than
(a) 900 mm (35 7/16″) above the highest point at
which the chimney comes in contact with the roof,
and (b) 600 mm (23⅝″) above the highest roof
surface or structure within 3 m (9′-10⅛″) of the
chimney.
Appendix note
Figure A-9.21.4.4.(1) shows the vertical and
horizontal distances from the chimney top to the
roof.
Both apply
The flue meets (a) and (b), so the higher of the
two tops governs.
Drawn: heights to the top of the flue liner, roof slope 6 in 12. Houses and chimneys are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.21.4.4. (page 9-159)
